I'm fine with repo staying under your account or creating organisation, just need more permissions for stuff like tokens if I'm expected to maintain publishing for all registries.

I'm not planning to abandon project (yet), even though I'm not as active in the project that originally brought me here ([lapce](https://github.com/lapce/lapce)).

So far I've been pacing myself to not dedicate completely (binge develop 24/7 as I used to do for other open source projects) so I don't burn out. Mostly giving bare minimum to keep project working and improve even if slightly, this is also because I'm mostly familiar with Rust, Linux and Docker so things like VS Code, JS/TS and npm are not my expertise (though I'm learning everything I can).

I can't promise anything long-term as I'm currently looking for work and a bit on tight deadline ($$$) so next month will be deciding factor :>

---

I'm currently the owner of the pypi package and can transfer it to whatever/whomever is going to maintain the project.

From what I know, GitHub organisation is required to give access for a team on crates.io, so if we want to go down that route, then making `taplo` organisation seems like the best solution.
The orgnization permission model is much more flexible IMO.

Thanks @tamasfe for all the efforts and care you've put into this project. This makes it all harder to decide to step down.

While I'm still not planning to help maintain this project, I believe this is an important project for the Rust community (for `Cargo.toml` formatting). That's why I'll give my opinion to try to maximize the project chances of success.

I agree with both @panekj and @JounQin that a GitHub organization should be preferred. My rationale is that the set of maintainers is going to change over time and no maintainer is expected to survive the project. So a GitHub organization will provide the maximum stability to the project.

If we don't find an initial set of maintainers or if we don't reach a good enough quota of commitment, we could ask https://users.rust-lang.org/ for help.

Thank you for everything @tamasfe! Taplo has been and still is a great project, even if there are things you wish you could improve.

While I have not personally contributed to this (yet), I would like to echo that moving to an organization is probably for the best.

To help attract new contributors, it would also be amazing to try and flesh out some of the ideas you have above. In my experience, creating an overarching tracking issue (like [I have done in Pact-Python](https://github.com/pact-foundation/pact-python/issues/396)) can provide a lot of help for new contributors to see what they can/should contribute to. This would really help pass on all the stuff you have thought of and help make it concrete for others to take over (though it is still a fair bit of work to create such a tracking issue).

Thank you all for the input, it looks like an organization is the way to go then. I will try to set one up as well as collect ideas/thoughts/TODOs like @JP-Ellis suggested for a proper handoff before I disappear (again).

I'd like to suggest also reaching out to the rust-analyzer owners to see if there's some scope to pull this into their responsibility area. While this isn't purely a Rust specific tool, there's quite a bit of overlap in the techniques and goals between rust-analyzer and this that could benefit from some cross pollination.

Clearly a github org would help in the long run (I can confirm that personal accounts are limited). At the same time I would advise trying to reuse an existing github organization as this might help gathering other contributors and ease management, one that I found interesting might be https://github.com/toml-lang -- but the key question is if the current 3 members are willing to help this project transition there.

IMHO when picking an org this this preference should be looked into:

- `TOML` focused
- `development tooling` focused (to also allow hosting the vscode toml extension)
- `rust` focused

@tamasfe If you agree, mention the 3 members of @toml-lang in a comment here asking them if they want to help you with the transition. One requirement that will be needed is to allow others to be invited top the organization (ACLs based on teams limit access).

@tamasfe Thank you so much for your work and contributions to `jsonschema` - its external resolvers are used in `taplo`!

I recognize that `taplo` is one of the most significant users of the `jsonschema` crate, and I’m happy to take care of all `jsonschema`-related issues in `taplo` in whatever way you and others find useful.

It’s important to me that this project succeeds - not only because it’s valuable on its own (my colleagues and I use it), but also because it helps improve `jsonschema`. For example, I believe `taplo` would greatly benefit from async external schema retrieval, which I’d implement in `jsonschema` and then submit a PR here to replace the current implementation.

Let me know if this is something that interests you.
@tamasfe Also forgot to mention, but if there is anything I can help with to accelerate migration to GH org, please let me know.
Thank you, I think I'll just need a deep breath and a weekend, I wanted this done already, but might still take a while.

Life happens, thank you for the great extension.

I had some random toml extension error when looking at a Cargo.toml, then noticed the last release of EvenBetterTOML was in 2024, ig the curse of the toml extensions haha (the error is gone now though, no idea why).

Then I found a pretty unknown toml extension called tombi, see the mention above.
Maybe their structure is more useful for the stated goals / the maintainers can work together / cross-reference a bit?

Hello. I am the author of [Tombi](https://github.com/tombi-toml/tombi).

First of all, thank you @tomasfe for your great work.

I am currently developing a TOML Language Server inspired by taplo.

Tombi is inspired by Rust Analyzer, black, and taplo,
It is already at the stage where it can be used in my team's product development.

If interested, please use tombi and give me your feedback.

You will get a lot more visibility in the rust subreddit.
Open a call for contributors and you'll probably get many responses, many people want to contribute but don't know where to start.

Hi Tamás, hi everyone,

First, thank you @tamasfe for creating such a valuable tool. Even Better TOML and Taplo have become essential for many, including myself. I truly respect your transparency in this transition and the incredible work you've done bringing these tools to life with such polish.
I have been reaching out to Tamás directly over the past few weeks to discuss the possibility of taking over stewardship and ownership of the Even Better TOML VS Code extension. It is a tool I have been using and studying closely as part of an academic project, and it holds deep personal and professional importance to me. A few months ago, I started working on a project on a project with collaboration with an organization focused on open-source initiatives, and as someone committed to building tools for educational equity, I am very serious about the future of this tool.
I would like to express my interest in formally taking ownership and full maintenance responsibility of the VS Code extension, and if necessary, even the associated Taplo tooling.
 I am ready to own and maintain the plugin (Visual Studio Marketplace + Open VSX), keep it aligned with TOML updates, community needs, and performance expectations, modernize and document it with a focus on new contributors and student users.
And of course, offer compensation to facilitate this transition, in recognition of the groundwork laid and the responsibility involved.
If the idea of transferring the extension ownership is on the table, I would be grateful for the opportunity.

Thanks everyone.

Hello, a lot of time has passed and project did not move much (in my case due to health issues but I also didn't put much effort due to missing action on this issue). It would be nice to see an update regarding status of how to deal with the projects future.

In case it's not planned to "keep the project alive" or due to lack of any response, I'll use my tiny bit of power I have here (and the Visual Studio marketplace token that expires around 20th December) to push last update with notice that the project is unmaintained and people should not expect any updates or try to depend on it (or just to expect no further updates).

Hi, We've implemented format options in Tombi v0.6.47.
A series of feature developments are discussed [here](https://github.com/tombi-toml/tombi/issues/1117#issuecomment-3522968005).

We plan to create documentation that includes information about format options and migration steps from Taplo.

If you're interested in migrating from Taplo to Tombi,
would you be willing to provide feedback on the format options before we create the documentation?

@panekj 

Could you tell me a little more about why it can't be migrated?

- No information about who or what is developing Tombi, [bus factor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bus_factor) = 1
- I'm already familiar with Taplo codebase and have audited it, which I would have to repeat for Tombi
- Incompatible with Taplo, would require migrating configuration/tools
- Developed using LLMs

Thanks for the feedback!

> No information about who or what is developing Tombi, [bus factor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bus_factor) = 1

I did try to [seek co-owners](https://github.com/tombi-toml/tombi/discussions/648) before, but haven't been able to form a team successfully(I still seek it.). 
I think it's a common issue for many open-source projects started by individuals to lack developer info.

> I'm already familiar with Taplo codebase and have audited it, which I would have to repeat for Tombi

That's a strong reason to fork, since it's not something Tombi can solve on it.

> Incompatible with Taplo, would require migrating configuration/tools

We don't offer complete compatibility, so migration changes are expected, as is the case with most formatter switches.

> Developed using LLMs

While the majority of the code was written by me, I'm also experimenting with development that incorporates LLM assistance.
Considering that Tombi is a project with intricate components like an AST, I understand the hesitation some might have with the term "LLM."
(I was adding the 🦅 logo as a completion suggestion even before using LLMs, but it seems [users' reactions to emojis](https://github.com/tombi-toml/tombi/issues/1212) have completely changed 😅)
I'm developing Tombi with care to ensure it functions correctly, but continuous user observation is necessary regardless of LLM usage.
